subject: design-technology
title: Foundations: What Makes a Material Smart?
welcome_lead: Touch a colour-changing mug and discover the materials that respond to their environment.
meta_desc: Learn the definition of smart materials and key examples for GCSE D&T.
final_note: You can define a smart material and give examples of inputs that trigger them.

concepts.def: Material whose property changes with a stimulus.
Returns to a remembered shape when heated.
Generates voltage when squeezed or vibrated.

walkthroughs.body_html: A smart material changes one of its properties — shape, colour, stiffness, charge — when a stimulus is applied. The change is reversible in many cases, so the same material can be used again and again.
Thermochromic inks colour-change with heat (mood rings, kettles). Photochromic lenses darken in sunlight. Piezoelectric crystals turn pressure into voltage (lighter sparks, microphones).
Spectacle frames made from Nitinol bend out of shape but return when warmed by body heat. This shape memory effect makes them nearly indestructible during normal wear.
